back: A parameter describes a population (often unknown). A statistic is calculated from a sample to estimate it.
Categorical: groups (nominal or ordinal). Quantitative: numerical values (discrete or continuous).
Nominal: category order does not matter (payment method). Ordinal: order matters (satisfaction level).
Discrete: specific set of values (number of apps). Continuous: any value in a range (screen time).
Representative, randomly selected and large enough. Larger samples tend to have smaller sampling error.
Simple random, systematic (every nth), stratified (random from each subgroup), cluster (random clusters, sample all).
Stratified: sample within every subgroup. Cluster: pick some clusters and sample every member in them.
Nonresponse bias (many fail to respond) and response bias (anything in the survey that influences answers).
Complicated (double-barreled), vague, leading, central tendency bias, error-prone options, voluntary response.
Proportion = count / total (0 to 1). Percentage = proportion × 100%. Sample p̂, population p.
Pie: categories do not overlap and show parts of a whole (max ~6). Bar: overlap or partial categories allowed.
Counts sum to n. Relative frequencies sum to 1 (or 100%) when categories do not overlap.
x̄ = (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ)/n. Estimates population mean μ. Example: 480/6 = 80.
s = √[Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1)]. Estimates σ. Example profits 65 to 97 give s ≈ 11.8.
s² = Σ(x − x̄)²/(n − 1). Squared units, so use the standard deviation to interpret.
Z = (x − x̄)/s. Number of standard deviations from the mean. Positive: above mean; negative: below.
Multiply data by a: mean and s multiply by a. Add a: mean shifts by a; s is unchanged.
C_V = s/|x̄|. Heterogeneous if above 30%. Used to compare spread across different scales.
More than 3 standard deviations from the mean (Z-score beyond ±3).
Resistant: little affected by extremes (median, IQR). Sensitive: mean and standard deviation.
Shape (symmetric, right or left skewed), modality (unimodal, bimodal, uniform) and outliers. Normal: bell-shaped.
q_a = x₍ₐ·ₙ₎, rounding a·n up when it is not an integer. Example: 0.25 × 19 = 4.75, so use x₍₅₎.
Odd n: x₍(n+1)/2₎. Even n: average of x₍n/2₎ and x₍n/2+1₎. Example: 20 wages give 77.5.
Range = max − min. IQR = Q₃ − Q₁ (spread of the middle 50%). Example: 99 − 32 = 67; 84 − 66 = 18.
Outlier if below Q₁ − 1.5 × IQR or above Q₃ + 1.5 × IQR. Example: cutoffs 39 and 111 flag 32.
Min, Q₁, median, Q₃, max. Box from Q₁ to Q₃, line at median, whiskers to the extreme non-outliers.
r = s_xy/√(s²ₓ·s²_y). Near +1 or −1 is a strong linear link; correlation is not causation.
b₁ = s_xy/s²ₓ = r·s_y/sₓ; b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄; prediction ŷ = b₀ + b₁x.
R² = r² in simple regression: share of the variability in y explained by x.
